=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: ".claude/hooks/session-start.sh: when the merge changes `.claude/settings.json`, the session records that the new wiring applies from the next session." (Issue #4952, G3 in docs/plans/issue-4952-sync-claude-assets-at-session-start-plan.md:24) and "Step 6 of the Claude-asset sync runs the check whenever the sync merge changed `settings.json`. Current → continue. Not current (after one re-run) → no further commit, push, claim, comment, label change, or dispatch for that work in this session" (docs/plans/issue-5259-restart-after-settings-sync-plan.md:33-37).
  expected_change_site: `.claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md` step 5
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md` step 5 at line 47-49 says "When the sync's step 6 check cannot confirm that this session loaded the merged `settings.json`, do not fix or push here: follow its [Settings restart]". The Settings restart does start a fresh session, but the original session is now in the same "do not commit / push / claim / comment / label change / dispatch / wait" state that the new command prose requires. The `/fix-claude-pr` step 5 does not enumerate that prohibition for itself — it defers entirely to the Settings restart path, which is fine, but the implementation in the new session needs to verify (re-read the check) before any push of its own merge commit. The current text says "follow its [Settings restart]" but does not say "in this command, before pushing the sync's merge commit, re-verify the loaded settings"; the risk is that the original fixer pushes the sync merge commit before the fresh session is created, which contradicts the plan's "no further commit, push, claim, comment, label change, or dispatch for this work" rule.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
